plain_title: When ejaculation keeps happening sooner than you want
one_liner: Ejaculating within about a minute of penetration, before you want to, most of the time, for six months or more.
in_simple_words: Premature or early ejaculation is when ejaculation regularly happens sooner than a person or couple wants, typically within about a minute of penetration, most of the time for at least six months, and it bothers them. It can be lifelong or start later. Timing varies hugely between people, and this is only a problem when it causes distress. It's among the most common sexual complaints, and behavioural techniques, psychosexual therapy, and medication prescribed by a doctor all help.
what_it_can_feel_like: I avoided dating for years because of it. A sex therapist gave me a plan, and it turned out I wasn't broken.
We treated it as our problem, not his. That took most of the shame out of the room.
common_signs: Ejaculation within about a minute of penetration, most of the time
Little or no sense of being able to delay it
Distress, frustration, or avoiding sex because of it

myths_vs_facts.myth: It's a sign of selfishness or lack of self-control.
myths_vs_facts.fact: Timing is largely about reflexes, nerves, and anxiety, not character. It's a treatable condition, not a character flaw.

myths_vs_facts.myth: Nothing can be done except distraction tricks.
myths_vs_facts.fact: Structured behavioural techniques taught by a therapist and medication prescribed by a doctor have good evidence, especially combined.

how_common.plain: Surveys suggest about 1 in 5 to 1 in 3 men report ejaculating earlier than they'd like, but the stricter lifelong form affects around 2 to 5 in 100.
how_common.figure: Self-reported PE 20%–30%; lifelong PE under 1–2 minutes about 2%–5% (2019 review)

what_helps.plain_summary: The best results come from combining approaches: behavioural techniques taught in psychosexual therapy, which train awareness and control, and help for anxiety; and medication, prescribed and monitored by a doctor, that delays ejaculation, either taken daily or before sex depending on the drug and country. Treating erectile problems if they coexist matters, since worry about losing an erection can speed things up. Partners are usually included where there is one.
evidence_based_options: Medication to delay ejaculation, prescribed and monitored by a doctor
Treatment of coexisting erectile difficulty or anxiety
self_help_that_supports_care: Reading reputable guides rather than forums selling 'cures'
Talking openly with a partner; shared, not solo, problem
Reducing performance pressure: not every encounter has to end a certain way

when_to_reach_out: If early ejaculation is upsetting you or your relationship, or you're avoiding sex because of it, talk to a doctor or a psychosexual therapist. It's common and there are real options.
is_not: Sexual difficulties that are occasional, explained by a medical condition or medication, caused by severe relationship distress, or that don't bother you aren't diagnosed as a disorder. Faster ejaculation after a long gap, with a new partner, or when very aroused is normal.
hope_note: Most people gain control with treatment. Many say the biggest change was dropping the shame.

content_notes: Sex-positive, shame-free wording; no explicit technique descriptions. Medication named only in general terms.
